title: Row-minor ideals of submodules under scalar extension
statement:
Let $R,A$ be commutative rings, let $\varphi:R\to A$ be a ring homomorphism, let $n,r\ge0$, and let $K\subseteq R^{\oplus n}$ be any $R$-submodule [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Let $K_A\subseteq A^{\oplus n}$ consist of the finite sums $\sum_{\alpha}a_\alpha\varphi(z_\alpha)$, where $a_\alpha\in A$, $z_\alpha\in K$, and $\varphi$ is applied coordinatewise. For a commutative ring $B$ and submodule $L\subseteq B^{\oplus n}$, let $E_r^B(L)$ be the ideal generated by the determinants [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] of the $r\times r$ submatrices [def-weil-submatrix] of all $r\times n$ matrices [def-weil-matrix] with rows in $L$; set $E_0^B(L)=B$ and $E_r^B(L)=0$ if $r>n$.
The canonical $A$-linear map
$$\theta:R^{\oplus n}\otimes_R A\longrightarrow A^{\oplus n},\qquad x\otimes a\longmapsto (a\varphi(x_j))_j$$
[def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-module-base-change] is an isomorphism, with inverse $(a_j)_j\mapsto\sum_j e_j\otimes a_j$, where $e_j$ is the standard basis. It carries the image of $K\otimes_R A\to R^{\oplus n}\otimes_R A$ onto $K_A$. Moreover,
$$E_r^A(K_A)=\varphi(E_r^R(K))A.$$
Here the right side is the ideal generated by the image under $\varphi$. No flatness of $A$ over $R$ or finite generation of $K$ is assumed.

Its pure-tensor formula, followed by tensor commutation and Algebra.smul_def, gives the stated coordinates. Decompose a coordinate vector as the finite sum of its single-coordinate vectors using [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Linearity and piScalarRight_symm_single give the inverse formula after commuting the tensor factors. This also handles n=0.

proof.text: The tensor image of the inclusion is Submodule.baseChange. Mathlib Submodule.baseChange_eq_span identifies it with the A-span of the vectors 1 ⊗ z for z in K; this is the finite-sum description from [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and [def-weil-module-base-change]. Transport this equality by the coordinate linear map and apply Submodule.map_span. The coordinate formula on 1 ⊗ z identifies the resulting generating set with the coordinatewise images of elements of K. No injectivity of the tensor inclusion is used.

proof.text: Prove the ideal equality first for rowMinorIdeal n k and arbitrary k. If n ≤ k, both sides are the unit ideal. Otherwise set q=n-k. Applying a ring homomorphism to a determinant [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] commutes with the determinant, by RingHom.map_det. Extracting any selected rows preserves membership in K, and taking all rows of such a q-row matrix and a chosen q-column subset gives a defining minor generator.

source.place: Tag 07ZA (lemma-fitting-ideal-basics), proof of (3); Tag 07Z8 (lemma-fitting-ideal), kernel-row description; explicit scalar-extension calculation supplied here.

proof.text: For the inclusion from the mapped ideal into the new row-minor ideal, use Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap. Reduce through the defining suprema and ideal spans to a minor of a matrix with rows in K. Its image is the determinant of the matrix with coordinatewise image entries by Step 3. Those rows lie in the new A-span by Submodule.subset_span, so the image determinant is a generator of the new row-minor ideal.

source.place: Tag 07ZA (lemma-fitting-ideal-basics), proof of (3); Tag 07Z8 (lemma-fitting-ideal), kernel-row description; explicit scalar-extension calculation supplied here.

proof.text: For the converse inclusion, fix the selected column subset. Taking its coordinates and then the determinant [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] is an A-multilinear function of the q chosen relation rows, by detRowAlternating and compLinearMap. Membership of its value in an ideal extends from tuples of generating rows to tuples of rows in their span. Prove this by induction on the finite set of coordinates allowed to lie in the span. At an inserted coordinate, use Submodule.span_induction: a generating row follows from the induction hypothesis, the zero row gives determinant zero, addition gives a sum of determinants, and scalar multiplication gives the scalar multiple of a determinant. This implements finite rowwise distribution without selecting simultaneous finite expansions. The finite-set empty case is the original generating-row assertion.

source.place: Tag 07ZA (lemma-fitting-ideal-basics), proof of (3); Tag 07Z8 (lemma-fitting-ideal), kernel-row description; explicit scalar-extension calculation supplied here.

proof.text: For a tuple of generating image rows, choose its preimage rows in K (the asserted generating-set membership supplies them). Step 3 expresses its determinant as the image of the corresponding original minor, hence in the mapped ideal. Apply Step 5 to the rows of every new defining minor. Ideal.span_le and the defining suprema give the reverse inclusion. Combining the two inclusions proves the equality for all k. Finally put k=n-r when r≤n; for r>n both displayed ideals are zero. No finite generation, flatness, or choices from an unproved existence theorem occur.

lean.statement: theorem rowMinorIdeal_scalar_extension {R : Type u} {A : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (n r : ℕ) (K : Submodule R (Fin n → R)) : ∃ θ : (A ⊗[R] (Fin n → R)) ≃ₗ[A] (Fin n → A), (∀ (x : Fin n → R) (a : A), θ (TensorProduct.comm R (Fin n → R) A (x ⊗ₜ[R] a)) = fun j : Fin n ↦ a * algebraMap R A (x j)) ∧ (∀ a : Fin n → A, TensorProduct.comm R A (Fin n → R) (θ.symm a) = ∑ j : Fin n, (Pi.single j 1 : Fin n → R) ⊗ₜ[R] a j) ∧ (Submodule.map θ.toLinearMap (LinearMap.range (K.subtype.baseChange A)) = Submodule.span A (Set.range (fun z : K ↦ fun j : Fin n ↦ algebraMap R A (z.val j)))) ∧ (if n < r then (⊥ : Ideal A) else rowMinorIdeal n (n - r) (Submodule.span A (Set.range (fun z : K ↦ fun j : Fin n ↦ algebraMap R A (z.val j))))) = Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) (if n < r then (⊥ : Ideal R) else rowMinorIdeal n (n - r) K)
